name_zh: 科威特·贾比尔：石油福利议会与伊拉克入侵解放
name_en: Kuwait Jaber: Oil Welfare Parliament & Iraq Invasion Liberation
description_zh: 贾比尔·艾哈迈德·萨巴赫 (1926-2006) 科威特埃米尔 (1977-2006)，石油财富建立高福利议会制，1990年伊拉克入侵触发海湾战争，美国领军联军解放，战后重建确立小国安全依赖大国保护伞现实。
description_en: Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah (1926-2006) Kuwait Emir (1977-2006), oil wealth built high-welfare parliamentary system, 1990 Iraq invasion triggered Gulf War, US-led coalition liberated, post-war reconstruction established small state security reliance on great power protection umbrella reality.
reason_zh: 贾比尔代表海湾小国如何通过石油福利换取国内合法性、通过大国保护伞换取生存安全，展示了议会制在威权传统中的有限运作，其被入侵与解放经历定义了海湾安全架构核心逻辑。
reason_en: Jaber represents how Gulf small state exchanges oil welfare for domestic legitimacy and great power umbrella for survival security, demonstrating parliamentary system limited operation in authoritarian tradition, his invasion and liberation experience defining Gulf security architecture core logic.
steps_zh: 研究贾比尔早年统治家族成员与1963年首个民选议会
分析石油收入支撑免费医疗教育住房福利国家
探讨1990年伊拉克入侵与科威特流亡政府外交
评估1991年沙漠风暴行动解放与战后环境灾难
总结石油福利议会伊拉克入侵解放对海湾小国安全模式的定型
steps_en: Study Jaber early ruling family member and 1963 first elected parliament
Analyze oil revenue supporting free healthcare education housing welfare state
Explore 1990 Iraq invasion and Kuwait exile government diplomacy
Evaluate 1991 Desert Storm liberation and post-war environmental disaster
Summarize oil welfare parliament Iraq invasion liberation shaping Gulf small state security model
expected_zh: 掌握石油福利与大国保护双重支柱如何构成海湾小国生存逻辑，理解议会制在部落威权中的有限空间，评估科威特模式对卡塔尔巴林阿联酋等邻国的示范与局限。
expected_en: Master how oil welfare and great power protection dual pillars constitute Gulf small state survival logic, grasp parliamentary system limited space in tribal authoritarianism, evaluate Kuwait model demonstration and limits for Qatar Bahrain UAE neighbors.
case_zh: 1977 埃米尔；1990 入侵；1991 解放；2006 逝世。石油福利议会伊拉克入侵解放范式永存。
case_en: 1977 Emir; 1990 invasion; 1991 liberation; 2006 death. Oil welfare parliament Iraq invasion liberation paradigm endures.
cross_cultural_impact: Oil welfare state; Gulf War; parliamentary monarchy; liberation
